# Shruti 1.4.12
A clarity and safety release. Nothing about how Shruti sounds has changed: the direct path is still bit-transparent and processing still costs only what its badge says. What changed is that Shruti no longer surprises you — a window control cannot silently stop your audio service, a broken service tells you how to fix it, and the mixer says one name for one thing.
## Closing a window no longer quits Shruti
- The floating (torn-off) panel's close button collapses it back into the menu bar, which is exactly what the pin button beside it does. Previously the close button quit the whole app and uninstalled the background audio service — from a standard macOS window control, with the menu bar icon still sitting there. - That mattered beyond the surprise: stopping the service hands every controlled app back to macOS at its own volume, **including a muted one**. A silent app becoming audible is the exact failure the emergency-bypass path is written to prevent, and a stray window close could cause it. It cannot any more. - Quitting is still a real full stop, and still available deliberately: **More → Quit Shruti & Stop Audio Service**. - Logging out, restarting or shutting down no longer uninstalls the service agent. macOS stops the job itself as part of closing the session, and Shruti's service is back at the next login instead of waiting for something to reinstall it. - "Pinned" is honoured at launch. The preference used to outlive the window: the pin button came back lit with no panel anywhere on screen.
## A service that is offline now tells you how to fix it
- When the audio service is not answering, every Shruti surface shows what that means for your sound — your apps are on macOS's normal path, nothing is muted, boosted or processed — with a **Repair** button in the same place. The route back used to be Settings → Health → Setup Assistant → Repair: four steps, documented only in the Support Centre, at the exact moment the product looks broken.
## One name for one control
- The panel button, the More menu, the Support Centre and VoiceOver now all call the global control **Bypass All**. The button reads `BYPASS ALL` when it is off and `BYPASSED` when it is on, so the label describes either the action or the state, never both. "True Bypass" now means the per-app power button and nothing else. - In AppleScript, the Shortcuts actions and the `shruti` command line this same control keeps its existing name, Stage Mode, so no saved script or shortcut breaks. The Support Centre says so. - The menu bar icon no longer glows amber while Bypass All is on. Amber means "Shruti is in this audio path", and a muted app legitimately keeps its tap under Bypass All — so the bypass shield used to light up amber at the one moment the whole promise is that Shruti is out of the way. It is now the same green the panel's `BYPASSED` button uses.
## A quieter, faster mixer
- App icons are resolved once instead of on every repaint. Each row used to perform a Launch Services lookup and an icon rasterization inside its view body, so they ran again for every row on every status poll, every hover and every frame of a slider drag — and fifty times per keystroke in the Add App list. That work is now done once per app. - The colour tile behind each app icon is a quiet backing plate rather than a full-strength gradient with a coloured glow. The real app icon sits larger and reads first; the colour survives as a rim and a wash, and a long list no longer carries a shadow layer per row. - **Remove** is no longer a permanently visible destructive button sitting beside the favourite star at the same weight as the volume controls. It appears when the row is under the pointer or is the keyboard-selected row, its space is always reserved so nothing shifts, and it remains permanently in the row's right-click menu — which is also how VoiceOver reaches it. It still asks for confirmation. - The `LEVEL BOOST` column heading was wider than its column and clipped. It reads `BOOST`, which is what the control under it does.
## Compatibility
Shruti 1.4.12 supports macOS 14.2 or newer and ships universal Apple silicon and Intel binaries. 510 product, safety, DSP and real-time checks pass, including the eight-app real-time budget at a 512-frame buffer.
